memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Lot looked around and saw that the whole plain of the Jordan toward Zoar was well watered, like the garden of the Lord, like the land of Egypt. (This was before the Lord destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah.) So Lot chose for himself the whole plain of the Jordan and set out toward the east. The two men parted company. - Gen 13:10-11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Lot looks, and he likes what he sees. Well-watered land, lush and green - it looked "like the garden of the Lord." So he takes it. Notice how the choice is made: entirely by sight. Lot never asks God. He never considers anything beyond what his eyes can measure. He simply looks and grabs.

Scripture drops in a chilling parenthesis: "This was before the Lord destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah." What looked like paradise was sitting on the edge of judgement. Lot's eyes could see the water; they could not see the future. That is always the limitation of choosing by sight alone.

Notice too the comparison: the land looked "like the land of Egypt" - the place Abram had just fled. And Lot "set out toward the east," the direction of drifting all through Genesis. Every detail whispers that this was a choice made away from God.

We make Lot's mistake constantly. We evaluate opportunities by what they look like - the salary, the comfort, the visible advantage - without asking God or considering what we cannot see. But "we live by faith, not by sight" (2 Cor 5:7). Before your next big decision, ask more than "How does it look?" Ask, "What does God say?" Your eyes cannot see what's coming. He can.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you make big decisions by what looks best, or by seeking God?
- What might you be unable to see about a choice in front of you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, forgive me for choosing by sight and forgetting to ask You. Give me eyes of faith. Before I decide, teach me to seek Your voice above what merely looks good.
Amen.
